Aveed (undecanoate injection) and Testopel (pellets) are not printed; they are provider-administered and may sit under the medical benefit (PDF p.5), so NOT recorded as nonformulary. Brand-name products not printed are recorded nonformulary under the closed-list statement (PDF p.2). Sig is standard label dosing. criteria: Primary hypogonadism (testicular failure) or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, AND two morning testosterone levels below reference range at separate times before treatment, OR a low or in-range level on treatment.

criteria: Diagnosis of primary hypogonadism (cryptorchidism, bilateral torsion, orchitis, orchiectomy, Klinefelter's, chemotherapy, toxins) OR hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (GnRH/LH deficiency, pituitary-hypothalamic injury).
Two morning total or free testosterone levels below the lab reference range at separate times before treatment, OR a level below or within range while already on treatment.
Metastatic breast cancer and delayed male puberty indications apply to testosterone enanthate only.

records.verificationNote: Tier 3 and PA for testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL read by x-coordinate on page 67. The guide prints no PA criteria, so the reason is the PA flag alone. Every other testosterone product in the guide needs PA, so cypionate is the lowest-barrier pick. Partial because injections may be self-administered under Part D or given in a clinic under Part B; the cost path is unconfirmed. Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Xyosted, Aveed, Androderm, Natesto, Testopel and methyltestosterone do not appear in the guide. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). All testosterone rows (cypionate, enanthate, 1.62% gel packet and pump) are on page 67. Cypionate is Tier 3 with PA and no BvsD flag; enanthate is Tier 3, PA, QL 25 per 90 days; the 1.62% gels are Tier 4 with PA. Cypionate stays the pick: it is the standard generic injectable and carries the same PA as every other listed product, unlike oral methyltestosterone, which is not listed. Part B applies only to clinic-administered injections, so the cost path stays unconfirmed (partial).] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary (exported 2026-11-02)] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary (reused, checked)] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary (reused, checked)]
